title: Objects and materials
keyIdea: An object is a thing; a material is what the thing is made of.

kid: A spoon is an object. It can be made of metal, wood or plastic. Those are materials.
It is still a spoon, whatever it is made of.
adult: Children often mix up objects (spoon, chair, window) with materials (metal, wood, glass). Ask 'what is it?' for the object and 'what is it made of?' for the material.
The same object can be made of different materials, and the same material can make many objects. That idea leads to choosing materials for a job.

familyTip: Pick three things in the kitchen. For each, say the object and the material: 'a cup, made of china'.

practice.explain: Wood is a material; chairs and tables are objects.

practice.prompt: {n} spoons are made of metal and {m} of wood. How many spoons?
{n} cups are plastic and {m} are glass. How many glass cups?

pool.prompt: Can a spoon be made of wood?

pool.explain: A chair is the object; wood is the material.

pool.prompt: There are {n} wooden blocks and {m} plastic blocks. How many blocks?
{n} toys are metal. {m} are not. How many toys?
Is plastic an object or a material?
pool.hint: Can you make things from it?

pool.prompt: A metal spoon and a wooden spoon are both…
pool.explain: Both are spoons, made of different materials.

visual.caption: Pick an object, then change its material. Is it still the same object?
